summary:
[FRAGMENT] 

[...] victims, and helpless. Their brave humor and good spirits in the face of the ghastly destruction of their brains is something wonderful; I put in all the funny stuff I could ... but as the novel progresses the funny stuff drains away. I, and the lead character, in fact all of us—we did the best we could to keep our flag­ ging spirits up. It’s amazing we did as well as we did, considering what became of us; them in living in, me in writing it. 

Your comments of my speech in paragraphs two and three on page two of your letter are brilliant, and I am reluctantly forced to come around and agree with them. This is not pleasant for me, to be forced out of my sentimentality, but you have done it, as has no one else, just in two paragraphs. I take off my hat to you, Göran; you are right and I yield. 

I wish you and I could get together again somewhere sometime; we evi­ dently are not going to Poland—Lem is acting very odd in what he is saying in his letters to me, so it probably will not work out after all. And our baby is due in mid-July; that will (already does) tie us down, here in Fullerton. But we are very happy, Tessa and I. And very busy. I also sold a new story, to Ferman and Malzbergl’s] new anthology, FINAL STAGE. So I’ve written and sold a story and two novels this year—after not being able to write during two terrible entire years.
